This confirms the pattern across the package. I now have enough evidence to finalize the assessment.

[{"id": "C04", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION lines 10-17: multi-sentence paragraph ('Fits penalised multi-task learning models... Supports multi-task regression, classification and censored survival data... Also provides elastic-net sparsity, parallel cross-validation, bootstrap inference, data simulation and plotting utilities.'), not a single line."},
{"id": "C08", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION line 12-13: 'following Vervier et al. (2014) <doi:10.1007/978-3-662-44845-8_18>'; also R/orthoMTL.R lines 81-85 use \\doi{10.1007/978-3-662-44845-8_18}."},
{"id": "C13", "verdict": "NON_COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION line 6: maintainer email is 'kevin.vervier@novartis.com', a corporate/employer domain tied to current employment rather than a durable personal address; such addresses risk becoming invalid if the maintainer changes employer."},
{"id": "C18", "verdict": "NOT_APPLICABLE", "evidence": "No \\dontrun{} tags found anywhere in man/ or R/ (grep for 'dontrun|donttest' returned no matches), so there is nothing to evaluate for justified vs unjustified \\dontrun{} use."},
{"id": "L06", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION text (lines 10-17) contains no unexpanded acronyms; terms like 'multi-task learning' are spelled out in full rather than abbreviated."},
{"id": "L08", "verdict": "NON_COMPLIANT", "evidence": "R/metrics.R:24: 'A patient is considered \"uncensored\" only if all task labels are non-NA.' -- double quotes used for emphasis on an ordinary word, not a publication title."},
{"id": "L09", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION lines 10-17 describe the package's overall functionality (multi-task regression/classification/survival, elastic-net, cross-validation, bootstrap, simulation, plotting) rather than naming/describing only the orthoMTL() wrapper function."},
{"id": "L10", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION lines 10-17 gives specific methodological detail (orthogonality/disjoint-support penalties, citation, survival-to-binary-task conversion, elastic-net, CV, bootstrap, simulation, plotting) rather than a thin one-line description."},
{"id": "L12", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "R/orthoMTL-package.R lines 82-86 and R/orthoMTL.R lines 81-85 contain @references sections citing Vervier et al. (2014) with doi; inst/CITATION also provides bibentry records for the implemented methods."},
{"id": "L21", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "DESCRIPTION line 4: 'Version: 0.1.0' and NEWS.md line 1/3: '# orthoMTL 0.1.0' / '* Initial CRAN submission.' -- version reflects a first release, not artificially inflated."},
{"id": "L23", "verdict": "NOT_APPLICABLE", "evidence": "No \\dontrun{} or \\donttest{} tags exist in any Rd/roxygen examples (grep across man/ and R/ found no matches), so there is no wrapped example to judge for run time."},
{"id": "L27", "verdict": "COMPLIANT", "evidence": "Examples use small synthetic data, e.g. R/orthoMTL.R:92 'n <- 100; p <- 10; n_tasks <- 3', R/cv_orthoMTL.R:81 'n <- 50; p <- 5; n_tasks <- 3', R/bootstrap.R:86 'n <- 30; p <- 5; n_tasks <- 3', R/simulate.R:109 'sim <- simulate_mtl(n = 100, p = 20, n_signals = 4, seed = 42)' -- all sized for syntax demonstration, not scale."}]
